main.result_summary: I consolidated week 2001-W26 (25–29 Jun) and made one commit on `main`; both gates (`lint.py` and `sleep-audit.py`) were green before it went in. I did not push, as the run brief says the runner does that after its own checks. The week had 75 messages, 63 of them with notes, and all 63 are cited in L1, so `dataset/drops/sleep-087.tsv` is empty. They went into five new files: talks and courses (the London course 28–29 Jun with Stig Faltinsen as the owner's guest, the EPIS conference 12–14 Sep, a baseball game during the Houston course 16–17 Jul, Ed Krapels, Darrell Duffie's expert report, a new Rice course), staff and admin (owner off 5, 6 and 9 Jul, his friend's job referral, intern dinner 2 Jul, office space decided in Aug–Sep), models (the bid-ask spread sessions, the convolution memo, the country forecast curves), requests and vendors (a 90% chance the Dabhol power contract ends in arbitration, Algorithmics meeting to be rescheduled, Helyette Geman's software contract), and a personal file for the London week. Four people reached five noted messages this week and now have entity files: Pushkar Shahi, William Stuart III, Eric Cope and Chris Calger. One message names "Euford Cooper (Ford)"; that isn't an exact match for the existing Ford Cooper file, so I left it unlinked and added an alias question to `questions.md` (due 2001-07-29). No question was past due. The compression quota had nothing to act on because no file was above 90% of its ceiling; the new talks file came out over the ceiling at 2871 characters and I cut it to about 2370 before committing. The five oldest ongoing lines are still valid. There were no sleep-task or feedback blocks, and `state.md` and the four domain indexes are updated. The runner's transcript file `dataset/runs/sleep-087.transcript.jsonl` is left uncommitted.
